newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County says to appeal welfare ruling.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County says to appeal welfare ruling.

text.p: Los Angeles County supervisors have decided to appeal a court order that could force the county to pay out $160 million in retroactive welfare benefits, a county spokeswoman said on Friday.
Last week, a state court of appeal ordered the county to pay retroactive benefits to general relief welfare recipients, whose grants were cut by $73 per recipient monthly from 1993 to 1995.
Attorneys involved in the case said Los Angeles County could be liable to pay up to $160 million if the appeals court decision stood.
After meeting in closed session, the county Board of Supervisors agreed to file an appeal to the state's Supreme Court, county spokeswoman Judy Hammond said.
